title: KV shelf repack and soft-quarantine allocation strategy to reduce GPU fragmentation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Long-lived KV cache entries plus variable microbatch sizes cause high external fragmentation on GPU memory, leading to lower effective cache capacity and unexpected OOMs under bursty traffic. Continuous batching improves throughput but amplifies fragmentation because KV objects are pinned by active sequences and microbatches hold mixed lifetime tokens.

Goals:
- Reduce fragmentation tail without regressing p99 latency beyond the current SLOs.
- Maintain or improve effective cache hit-rate for typical RLHF and chat workloads.
- Ensure background compaction and repack operate safely under Dedicated and Private environments.

Proposed strategy (high level):
1) Shelf-based allocation: divide KV pool into logical "shelves" based on expected token lifetime and sequence class (short/medium/long). Allocation chooses the best-fit shelf to reduce mixing hot short-lived objects with long-lived ones.
2) Soft-quarantine pool: newly relocated or freed slabs land in a quarantine shelf for a configurable window (soft_quarantine_ms) where they are preferentially reused for allocations matching recent access patterns. This reduces repeated churn across shelves.
3) Repack windows and quantum: schedule low-priority repack passes in configurable windows (repack_window_ms) that move cold slots together to create large contiguous free spans. Repack is staged with an adjustable quantum to bound GPU memory and CPU IO usage.
4) Pin and age heuristics: introduce age-based pin expiration for KV references retained by stalled microbatches. Add backpressure signals from the batching layer to avoid pinning during controlled drain.
5) Backpressure-aware allocation: when free contiguous spans are scarce, allocation will prefer short-lived shelves and trigger immediate lightweight compaction that is safe in the fast path.
6) Continuous-batching alignment: coordinate microbatch lifetimes with repack windows using a small delay budget so that microbatches complete within an aligned epoch to minimize cross-epoch pinning.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive repack reduces fragmentation but increases background GPU work and may cause transient latency jitter. We limit this via repack quantum and CPU/GPU time budgets.
- Shelf partitioning reduces cross-contamination but reduces flexibility; we allow dynamic shelf resizing based on telemetry.

Telemetry and safety:
- Add metrics: shelf_occupancy, shelf_fragmentation_percent, repack_cycles, quarantine_hit_rate, age_pin_count, continuous_batch_alignment_miss.
- Telemetry-driven autotune: initial implementation exposes knobs, later iterate to let controller adjust shelf sizes and repack cadence.
- Safety: repack and relocation run with strict price-of-safety thresholds; if p99 latency or CUDA memory pressure crosses thresholds, compaction pauses and we fall back to evict-first policy.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation: end-to-end simulator shows >40% reduction in fragmentation metric (free-span fragmentation index) for mixed chat workloads compared to baseline
Perf: in canary, effective KV capacity increases by at least 20% without >5% increase in p99 latency
Stability: repack does not cause OOMs; background GPU utilization controlled under configured quantum
Observability: new metrics are exported and dashboards created in Console for per-shelf views
Rollout plan documented with safe rollback and feature flags for Dedicated and Private customers

implementation_notes: Allocator changes limited to GPU-side metadata layout and host-side scheduler; avoid changing on-disk model artifacts
Repack uses incremental copy with double-write safety: write relocated KV to new slot, update indirection map, then free old slot
Quota controller will enforce a repack_rate_limit (slots/sec) and an urgent_compact_threshold for emergency eviction
Design includes hooks for Dedicated autoscaler to temporarily expand KV pool during heavy repack operations
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): run simulator and bench on synthetic mixes; iterate on quantum knobs
Phase 2 (canary): enable on 5% of traffic in staging clusters with aggressive telemetry
Phase 3 (gradual): enable on 10%->30%->100% with automated rollback on thresholds
Phase 4 (optimize): enable telemetry-driven shelf resizing and add autotune controller
